messages:
maya (Support): 09:12 UTC - Escalation: customer 'NeptuneHealth' reporting intermittent 5xxs from hosted inference API /v1/generate starting ~09:10. ~15-25% of calls are returning 500/502. They pasted a few examples; I'm escalating to SRE and platform. 

ajay (SRE): 09:13 UTC - I see control-plane 5xx alert for us-east-1. Error rate jumped at 09:10 and peaked around 09:14. Correlated logs show multiple downstream timeouts: routing-policy-service timeout, session-store/auth lookups failing, and config-db connection pool exhaustion. 

ops-bot: 09:14 UTC - :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2026-3095 (linked to control-plane 5xx spike) :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: 09:14 UTC - Canary check: 3/5 control-plane canaries failing in us-east-1.

jess (Oncall): 09:15 UTC - Can someone paste a representative error body and a request-id? Also need a minimal repro curl so we can hit the same path from our debugging host.

maya (Support): 09:16 UTC - Customer sample body:
```json
{
  "error": "internal_server_error",
  "detail": "control_plane: routing-policy service timeout (deadline exceeded)",
  "request_id": "req-0a1b2c3d"
}
```
They also saw a second one: 
```json
{
  "error": "gateway_error",
  "detail": "auth/session lookup failed: connection reset",
  "request_id": "req-0a1b2c3e"
}
```

ajay (SRE): 09:17 UTC - From control-plane logs (snip):
```
2026-03-15T09:11:35Z control-plane routing-policy call timeout=15s err="context deadline exceeded" request_id=req-0a1b2c3d
2026-03-15T09:11:36Z auth/session lookup host=redis-us-east-1-1 err="read tcp 10.1.2.3:6379: connection reset by peer" request_id=req-0a1b2c3e
2026-03-15T09:11:37Z config-db pool exhausted active=200 max=200 waiters=37 service=routing-policy
2026-03-15T09:11:38Z routing-policy svc error upstream=postgres-us-east-1 err="timeout waiting for connection"
```

jess (Oncall): 09:18 UTC - Repro curl to run from infra-debug host: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
If you can run this from prod-debug1 in us-east and capture request_id that helps.

li (Platform Eng): 09:19 UTC - Quick diagnosis: routing-policy depends heavily on config-db for policy evaluation; if config-db connections are saturated routing-policy will block and hit timeouts which bubble up as control-plane 5xx. Also auth/session failures point to Redis flapping (maybe transient network). Short-term mitigation options: (1) enable routing-policy cached-decisions fallback (hot cache) to avoid DB lookups, (2) roll a small canary that bypasses routing-policy and uses last-known-good policy (3) increase config-db connection pool limit or add read replica. I can flip a fallback flag via console in ~5m.

kim (Eng-Infra): 09:20 UTC - Confirming DB host is RDS Postgres managed. Connection pool configured to 200 for routing-policy. We have evidence of bursting beyond pool with many concurrent requests (waiters=37). Immediate fixes: increase pool to 300 and scale instance class + add a read replica. I'll prepare change and a maintenance window note. Also investigating Redis cluster health for session-store; metrics show elevated cmdlat and occasional connection resets around the same time window.

ajay (SRE): 09:21 UTC - For fastest mitigation I recommend: 
- li enable routing-policy cached fallback (low risk)
- kim bump config-db pool cap + add a replica (moderate risk, takes ~10-15m)
- jess keep oncall until error rate back to baseline and confirm customer ack
I'll coordinate rolling restart of a routing-policy node if needed.

ryan (Customer Success): 09:22 UTC - Draft message to customer: "We're investigating intermittent 500 errors affecting calls to /v1/generate in us-east-1. We've identified a control-plane dependency issue and are applying mitigations (fallback routing + DB scaling). We'll share ETA in 20 minutes. Apologies for the disruption." Anyone want to edit before I send? :thumbsup:

maya (Support): 09:23 UTC - Customer agreed to temporary routing bypass. They can tolerate a short fallback to slightly older policy if it restores availability.

kim (Eng-Infra): 09:24 UTC - Applying immediate change: increase pool to 300 (routing-policy config) and spin up a read replica. Pushing now. Will post when done.

deploy-bot: 09:25 UTC - routing-policy config change applied to cluster routing-policy-prod-us-east-1 (version bump + pool=300).

li (Platform Eng): 09:26 UTC - Flipped feature flag: routing-policy.cached_fallback=true for us-east-1 (gradual rollout). Monitor shows decrease in DB queries from routing-policy nodes.

ajay (SRE): 09:28 UTC - Error rate dropping. Control-plane 5xx back to baseline by 09:27. Auth/session errors reduced after Redis broker failover; infra reports transient network issue to one Redis node and automated failover completed at 09:26.

ops-bot: 09:29 UTC - Incident INC-2026-3095 status: mitigation applied, monitoring.

jess (Oncall): 09:30 UTC - Keeping the follow-up window open 1h to confirm stability. Please collect the following for postmortem: request ids samples, DB pool metrics, Redis broker logs, routing-policy traces.

ajay (SRE): 09:31 UTC - Assignments: 
- kim (Eng-Infra): finalize DB replica + revisit pool sizing (ETA 2h)
- li (Platform Eng): implement permanent cached fallback / optimize routing policy to reduce DB chattiness (ETA 3d)
- jess (Oncall): run incident bridge notes and own aft postmortem doc (ETA draft 24h)
- maya/ryan (Support/CS): send customer post-incident update with mitigation summary and next steps (ETA 30m)
:thumbsup:

ryan (Customer Success): 09:32 UTC - Sent update to NeptuneHealth. They acknowledged and will monitor.

maya (Support): 09:33 UTC - Customer reported successful retries returned 200s. No further 5xxs seen from their side after 09:27.

ajay (SRE): 09:34 UTC - Closing immediate escalation. Will open a follow-up ticket for root cause and long-term fixes.

ops-bot: 09:35 UTC - Incident INC-2026-3095 marked as mitigated (mitigated_at=2026-03-15T09:27:12Z).

jess (Oncall): 09:40 UTC - Please upload logs and traces into the incident doc. Postmortem owner: ajay.

kim (Eng-Infra): 09:43 UTC - Post-mitigation note: increased DB pool to 300, added read replica, investigating autoscaling thresholds for DB. Also will run Redis cluster diagnostics.

ajay (SRE): 09:50 UTC - Next steps: full RCA (include network blip to Redis, DB pool exhaustion causing routing-policy head-of-line blocking). Likely contributing factor: sudden traffic spike from an internal churn job earlier at 09:09 that increased concurrent policy evals. We'll correlate ingress traffic from 09:05-09:15.

maya (Support): 09:55 UTC - Closing thread for now. Will reopen if customer sees recurrence. Thanks everyone.
